reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review contract, assessment rubric, fresh-review framework, DeviceMetric context, full DeviceMetric StructureDefinition report, deterministic aggregate, and local R4/R6 DeviceMetric definitions. Direct behavior reports were checked for `DeviceMetric` and had no direct findings; shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 DeviceMetric was FMM 1/trial-use, so the baseline compatibility burden is weak. That lowers the threshold for accepting a redesign, but it does not erase concern for central device association, lifecycle status, or patient-monitoring interpretation where wrong migration can attach a metric to the wrong device context.

overall.oneLineConclusion: DeviceMetric keeps its identity, but R6 remodels enough mandatory and central content that an explicit migration transform is unavoidable; preserving low-cost compatibility still matters, especially for source/parent to device.

reasoning.thesisMd: This is not a removed resource, but it is more than a set of isolated chores. R6 adds mandatory modifier `status`, replaces R4 `source`/`parent` with mandatory `device`, changes mandatory `category` from primitive code to CodeableConcept, and changes several optional but meaningful device-metric fields. A version relabel will fail for ordinary R4 instances, and correct migration needs policy for lifecycle status, device association, category wrapping, cadence interpretation, and some code mappings.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The resource identity and purpose remain recognizable, and unchanged fields such as identifier/type/unit continue to anchor the model. However, the local content model is broadly remodeled: every R4 instance has a primitive mandatory `category` that must be converted, every R6 instance needs a lifecycle `status`, and the central device relationship is renamed/consolidated into a required `device`. Optional populated fields add more transforms (`operationalStatus`, `color`, `measurementPeriod`, and calibration). The shape is therefore a major model remodel for migration planning even though it is not a resource replacement.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: The migration program is already unavoidable, so preventing one additional optional-field break is lower leverage than it would be for a mostly stable resource. But it is not zero leverage. Low-cost compatibility preservation, aliases, deprecated transitional elements, or precise migration guidance can still reduce safety risk and implementation cost, especially for the central device association and for value-set/code-system changes that otherwise require site-specific policy.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The most standards-review-worthy less-breaking alternative is for `source`/`parent` to `device`: retaining deprecated `source` and `parent`, or providing a transition rule, could preserve existing semantics while R6 adopts the simpler relationship model. For `status`, making the field optional would preserve legacy instances but undercut the R6 goal of explicit lifecycle modifier semantics. For `category`, `color`, and calibration, preserving primitive aliases would reduce wire breaks but create duplicate representations and precedence rules; these are mostly migration chores, with `color` relatively low-cost but also low safety value. For `measurementPeriod`, retaining both Timing and Quantity would preserve more data but risks contradictory cadence facts.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: No OperationDefinition, SearchParameter, or HTTP/REST behavior finding directly names DeviceMetric. The 11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings remain relevant to all resources as platform context, but they do not change this DeviceMetric-specific conclusion.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The deterministic aggregate concluded `Partial` with `moderate-targeted-remodel` and the same compatibility posture. I agree with the posture but rate unavoidability higher: the aggregate count does not fully capture the combined effect of a new required modifier, a required replacement device relationship, and mandatory category wire-shape conversion. These make a deliberate migration transform necessary for baseline R4 DeviceMetric content, not just for edge cases.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: The structural evidence is high confidence. The main uncertainty is implementation prevalence and official committee rationale; R4 FMM 1 means deployed reliance may be limited, but no local evidence proves it is absent.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds mandatory modifier `DeviceMetric.status` with no R4 element
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: A conformant R6 DeviceMetric cannot omit `status`, and its modifier semantics require consumers to inspect lifecycle state before relying on the metric. This forces every migration to assign or infer a status. The break is probably proportionate for FMM 1 content because it separates lifecycle validity from operational state, but it is a core reason migration is unavoidable.

findingConsiderations.title: R4 `source` and `parent` references are removed and replaced by mandatory `device`
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the main avoidable/safety-relevant concern. Mapping two R4 relationship slots to one required R6 `device` can be lossy and policy-dependent, and an incorrect device association can change how monitoring metrics are interpreted. Even with a broader migration program, this deserves standards attention or very explicit transition guidance.

findingConsiderations.title: `category` changes from required primitive code to extensible CodeableConcept
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Because `category` is mandatory in R4 and R6 but changes wire shape, every R4 instance requires conversion from a primitive code to CodeableConcept. Ordinary migration is mechanical because the core codes remain available, so this drives the resource-level migration requirement more than it drives a revisit recommendation.

findingConsiderations.title: `operationalStatus` required value set removes `entered-in-error` and adds `unknown`
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a real required-binding break for instances that used `entered-in-error`, but the R6 model has a clearer target in `status=entered-in-error`. It is a local terminology migration and probably acceptable if migration guidance makes the lifecycle-versus-operational split explicit.

findingConsiderations.title: `color` changes from R4 metric-color code to R6 CodeableConcept bound to color-codes
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is an optional display-oriented field, so it should not dominate the resource conclusion. A deprecated primitive alias would be a relatively low-cost compatibility measure, but the safety value is low and ordinary R4 colors can be mapped into the richer R6 color coding model.

findingConsiderations.title: `measurementPeriod` Timing is removed and replaced by `measurementFrequency` Quantity
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Populated R4 cadence data needs more than a simple rename because Timing can express schedules that are not equivalent to a single Quantity frequency. This can require human or device-profile policy, but retaining both fields in base R6 would create conflicting cadence representations.

findingConsiderations.title: Calibration type/state change from required primitive codes to extensible CodeableConcepts, with state code change
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Calibration can be safety-relevant when present, and populated R4 entries need code wrapping plus `unspecified` to `unknown` handling. Because the backbone and affected children are optional and the richer CodeableConcept pattern is coherent, this is mainly a migration-guidance item rather than a resource-level blocker.

findingConsiderations.title: Several formerly summary elements are no longer marked `isSummary` in R6
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The summary-flag changes can affect `_summary` payloads and generated summary views, but they do not invalidate instances or remove data from full reads. For FMM 1 DeviceMetric, this is discounted as runtime/tooling churn rather than a reason to alter the resource-level posture.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds optional `availability` with no R4 representation
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is additive for R4-to-R6 migration. It can cause reverse-direction information loss for new R6 content, but it does not contribute materially to unavoidable R4-to-R6 migration.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context can affect platform behavior around all resources, but it is not a DeviceMetric-specific behavior change and is therefore not scored into the DeviceMetric resource-level conclusion.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Revisit the `source`/`parent` to required `device` transition. If the R6 model is retained, provide normative-quality migration guidance for choosing the referenced device and handling R4 instances with both, one, or neither relationship.

Publish explicit DeviceMetric R4-to-R6 mapping guidance for assigning `status`, wrapping primitive `category`, `color`, and calibration codes as CodeableConcepts, moving `entered-in-error` from `operationalStatus` to `status`, and converting simple `measurementPeriod` Timing values to `measurementFrequency` Quantity.
Treat summary-flag differences and optional `availability` as documentation/downgrade considerations rather than blockers to the R6 DeviceMetric design.

caveats: The review is based on local R4/R6 definitions and generated reports, not external implementation telemetry.
R4 DeviceMetric FMM 1 weakens stability expectations; the safety discussion is based on plausible device-monitoring semantics rather than measured deployment prevalence.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered as context only because DeviceMetric is neither Resource nor DomainResource.
R6 input is ballot4, so final published R6 content may differ.
